feed.title: Below the Surface

bullets: Coral bleaching events are not random — recognizing their pattern is the foundational insight that makes subsequent conservation decisions easier.
Most reef damage from divers isn't fin contact but anchor strikes — a counterintuitive finding that shifts where conservation effort should focus.
Erosion in coastal areas drives sediment plumes, which crosscut reef conservation and marine biology — the framing matters because it reveals which tradeoffs are being made.
The second-order effects of adopting tools like PADI in reef management flows are the part most people miss — ignoring them leads to rebuilding systems from scratch a year later.
Outside of Suunto-class tooling, the failure mode in reef monitoring is harder to spot, making early detection of problems more difficult.
A practical heuristic for listeners: pick one idea from the conversation and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration.
